notes_measurement: Verbatim source sentence: 'The 2-4-h transient post-infusion partial thromboplastin time prolongation values, a class effect of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides, were 18, 21 and 23 s for 250, 300 and 350 mg, respectively.' 250 mg was the fixed dose for patients weighing 36-50 kg (>50 kg patients were randomised to 300 or 350 mg), so this is a weight-band group, not a randomised dose arm. GRADE RATIONALE: coagulation-time change is not a platelet endpoint and the source reports no platelet finding whatsoever, so this carries grade 0 and is_platelet_specific=FALSE - the same convention already used in this dataset for the Crooke 2016 aPTT rows (TMSR109-TMSR132). The grade-0 label here means 'no platelet event observed/reported at this exposure', NOT 'no coagulation effect'; the aPTT effect is real, transient, dose-ordered and explicitly labelled a PS class effect. UNIT AMBIGUITY, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: the sentence reads as the magnitude of prolongation in seconds (i.e. +18 s over baseline). It could conceivably be an absolute post-infusion PTT value, but 18 s would sit below a normal aPTT reference range (~25-35 s), which makes the increment reading far more likely. Recorded exactly as printed rather than converted or re-based. effect_vs_control is TBD because this was a single-arm dose-ranging trial with no placebo group and the abstract gives no baseline PTT.

notes_measurement: Verbatim source sentence: 'The 2-4-h transient post-infusion partial thromboplastin time prolongation values, a class effect of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides, were 18, 21 and 23 s for 250, 300 and 350 mg, respectively.' 350 mg is the highest dose studied and the reason this paper was selected as a high-exposure human PS-ASO locus. GRADE RATIONALE: coagulation-time change is not a platelet endpoint and the source reports no platelet finding even at the top dose, so grade 0 with is_platelet_specific=FALSE, matching the TMSR109-TMSR132 aPTT convention. NOTE FOR MODELLERS: the dose-ordered 18 -> 21 -> 23 s progression across 250/300/350 mg is the only dose-response signal the accessible text supports, and it is a coagulation, not a platelet, signal - do not let it be read as a platelet endpoint on the strength of the haematology adjacency. Same unit ambiguity as the other two rows (increment vs absolute PTT), recorded as printed. effect_vs_control TBD - single-arm, no placebo comparator.

effect_vs_control: increasing ISIS 2302 concentrations progressively eluted Factor H
source_table: Abstract (Results)
notes_measurement: IN-VITRO MECHANISM ROW — cell-free binding competition, NOT a platelet assay; grade 0 is a schema floor, not an observed platelet null. species=NA because the abstract does NOT state the species of the Factor H used; it was NOT assumed to be human, which matters because a human-source in-vitro row would otherwise be miscounted toward this lane's human-data priority. Verbatim basis: 'Direct interaction between ISIS 2302 and Factor H was demonstrated in a competition assay, where increasing concentrations of ISIS 2302 eluted Factor H from a heparin-sepharose column.' No concentrations, IC50 or elution percentages appear in the abstract, hence dose and readout_value TBD. Mechanistically this is polyanion competition for the heparin-binding site of Factor H — the same physicochemical PS-polyanion property invoked for platelet-protein binding, which is why the row is worth carrying despite not being platelet-specific.

notes_measurement: BLEEDING GRADED ON ATTRIBUTION, NOT ON THE KEYWORD — this row exists specifically so a keyword-driven reader does not mistake it for a grade-3 haemorrhagic event. Locus sentences: 'Other clinical observations included ... bruising in all dose groups throughout the study. Bruising was associated with a dose-dependent prolongation of clotting times, particularly activated partial thromboplastin times (APTT), that was transient in nature. Bruises occurred around site of intravenous dosing or blood collection, and were manifested as subcutaneous hemorrhages upon microscopic evaluation. There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' The authors therefore attribute the haemorrhage to a coagulation-cascade effect (aPTT prolongation, the well-known intrinsic-pathway effect of polyanionic PS oligonucleotides) and EXPLICITLY exclude a platelet-count cause in the very next clause. Per the rubric, grade 3 requires a haemorrhagic event ATTRIBUTABLE TO THROMBOCYTOPENIA; attribution here is explicitly to coagulopathy with normal platelets, so the thrombocytopenia grade is 0. is_platelet_specific=FALSE: adjacent-haematology fallback row, retained because the bleeding/no-thrombocytopenia dissociation is itself evidence for this endpoint. Dose recorded as the band 2-50 because the abstract says 'all dose groups' without a per-dose incidence; whether the 0 mg/kg vehicle group is included in 'all dose groups' is NOT resolvable from the abstract, and the localisation of bruises to IV dosing and blood-collection sites means a procedure-related component cannot be excluded. readout_value=TBD: no incidence, count or severity figure is printed.

notes_measurement: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, GRADE 0. Locus sentence: 'There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' Young adult cynomolgus monkeys, slow IV bolus every other day for 28 days (14 doses), dose levels 0, 2, 10 and 50 mg/kg/injection; basic group 3M+3F sacrificed 2 days after the last dose. Grade 0 per the rubric's 'no platelet signal at tested exposure'. readout_value=TBD because the abstract prints NO numeric platelet counts and the full text is paywalled — the finding is qualitative-only at this locus; a number here would be fabricated. The abstract makes a single blanket hematology statement covering the whole study rather than a per-dose breakdown, so this row and the 10 and 50 mg/kg rows all derive from that one sentence; they are split by dose group because the study genuinely ran three treated dose levels and the negative applies to each, but they are NOT three independent observations. The abstract's closing sentence independently corroborates this dose: '2 mg/kg ISIS 2302 produced no remarkable alterations.' Vehicle-control (0 mg/kg) row not emitted — no control platelet value is printed.

notes_measurement: HOW THE ON-TARGET/TOXICITY LINE WAS DRAWN: ARC1779 blocks the VWF A1 domain; in type 2B VWD the mutant VWF is hyperactive and clears platelets, so raising the platelet count IS the intended pharmacodynamic effect. This row is therefore NOT a toxicity signal and must not be read as one. It is retained because it is a human platelet-count measurement under 72 h of continuous systemic exposure (plasma ARC1779 76 ug/ml, range 59-130) in which platelet counts ROSE — i.e. no unintended drug-induced platelet-count fall was observed. Grade 0 = no platelet toxicity signal at the tested exposure. n=3 patients; values are medians with ranges as printed. Full regimen: 0.23 mg/kg IV loading dose then 4 ug/kg/min for 72 h; dose_or_conc_value carries the loading dose only because the infusion rate has no matching unit in the controlled vocabulary. Full text paywalled (Thromb Haemost / Thieme); abstract is the only locus available.

This is the cleanest danvatirsen monotherapy platelet signal available: platelet count decreased was the SINGLE most common adverse event, causally related to danvatirsen, in 60% of patients. Row therefore INCLUDED, with the mechanism recorded so a modeller can stratify on it. FIRST generation-2.5 (16-nt) compound in this dataset.

target_gene: multiple (APOC3, LPA, CFB, ANGPTL3, HBV S, KLKB1, AGT, GHR per Table 1)
design_source: doi:10.1089/nat.2018.0753 (PMC6386089) Table 1 + Supplementary Table S2
notes_oligo: PSEUDO-OLIGO / CLASS-LEVEL AGGREGATE, not a single compound. Every measurement row from this source is reported at this pooled level ('Total ASO' and dose-band columns of Table 5 / Supplementary Table S9), never per compound, so all rows carry this name. Table 1 covers 8 unique GalNAc3-conjugated PS 2'MOE ASOs, all 20-mers, all 5-10-5 MOE gapmers; 4 have a full-PS backbone (678354, 696844, 712408, 757456) and 4 a mixed PO/PS backbone (681257, 703802, 721744, 766720) - hence backbone_chemistry=mixed for the pool. Phase 1 HV-RCT totals from Table 1: 98 placebo + 294 active = 392 subjects. Supplementary Table S2 shows the weekly MULTIDOSE regimen cohort (N=157; 36 placebo + 121 ASO) draws on exactly 6 ASOs - HBV sAg 712408 (4 doses QW), GHR 766720 (4 doses BIW), Apo(a) 681257 (6 doses 3qod-QW), ApoCIII 678354 (6 QW), ANGPTL3 703802 (6 QW), FB 696844 (8 doses 2BIW-QW) - consistent with the 'Number of ASOs 6' row of Supplementary Table S5. KLKB1 721744 is excluded from the primary integrated analyses per Table 1 footnote b. Single-dose regimen cohort N=193 (50 placebo + 143 ASO) per Supplementary Table S9. Potency context (Results/Fig 3): ED50 4-10 mg/week for the GalNAc3 conjugates vs 120-210 mg/week for the unconjugated parents, i.e. up to 30-fold more potent. Platelet reference range used in these trials: 140-400 K/mm3 (Supplementary Table S1).
exposure_duration: 6 weekly SC doses (value at Dose 6, end of treatment)

Supplementary Table S5 footnote marks pairwise-vs-placebo change-from-baseline significance with */dagger/double-dagger; NO platelet cell in the table carries any such mark, so no dose band differed significantly from placebo. Contrast with unconjugated PS 2'MOE ASOs, where a dose- and plasma-concentration-dependent mean platelet decline is the characteristic signal.

target_gene: multiple (APOC3, LPA, CFB, ANGPTL3, HBV S, KLKB1, AGT, GHR per Table 1)
design_source: doi:10.1089/nat.2018.0753 (PMC6386089) Table 1 + Supplementary Table S2
notes_oligo: PSEUDO-OLIGO / CLASS-LEVEL AGGREGATE, not a single compound. Every measurement row from this source is reported at this pooled level ('Total ASO' and dose-band columns of Table 5 / Supplementary Table S9), never per compound, so all rows carry this name. Table 1 covers 8 unique GalNAc3-conjugated PS 2'MOE ASOs, all 20-mers, all 5-10-5 MOE gapmers; 4 have a full-PS backbone (678354, 696844, 712408, 757456) and 4 a mixed PO/PS backbone (681257, 703802, 721744, 766720) - hence backbone_chemistry=mixed for the pool. Phase 1 HV-RCT totals from Table 1: 98 placebo + 294 active = 392 subjects. Supplementary Table S2 shows the weekly MULTIDOSE regimen cohort (N=157; 36 placebo + 121 ASO) draws on exactly 6 ASOs - HBV sAg 712408 (4 doses QW), GHR 766720 (4 doses BIW), Apo(a) 681257 (6 doses 3qod-QW), ApoCIII 678354 (6 QW), ANGPTL3 703802 (6 QW), FB 696844 (8 doses 2BIW-QW) - consistent with the 'Number of ASOs 6' row of Supplementary Table S5. KLKB1 721744 is excluded from the primary integrated analyses per Table 1 footnote b. Single-dose regimen cohort N=193 (50 placebo + 143 ASO) per Supplementary Table S9. Potency context (Results/Fig 3): ED50 4-10 mg/week for the GalNAc3 conjugates vs 120-210 mg/week for the unconjugated parents, i.e. up to 30-fold more potent. Platelet reference range used in these trials: 140-400 K/mm3 (Supplementary Table S1).
exposure_duration: 4-8 SC doses over up to 6 weeks (weekly multidose regimen)
source_table: Table 5, Hematology block, Platelets row '<100 K/mm3, n (%)', '>0-10' dose column
notes_measurement: Dose band printed verbatim as '>0-10' under the header 'Dose categories, mg/week' - unit is mg PER WEEK, not a single total dose. Cell reads 0 (0.0); denominator n=32. This band brackets the stated ED50 range of 4-10 mg/week for the GalNAc3 conjugates, i.e. zero platelet signal at a fully pharmacologically active exposure. Zero severe-band cell: would have carried grade 2 had events occurred.

design_source: FDA_label_RYTELO_SPL_imetelstat;FDA NDA 217779 Orig1s000 Multi-discipline Review and Evaluation (imetelstat/Rytelo), Product Quality summary printed p39 and Clinical Pharmacology Executive Summary printed p76
notes_oligo: 13-mer lipid-conjugated N3'-P5' thiophosphoramidate telomerase template antagonist;NOT a PS-ASO;thrombocytopenia is on-target myelosuppression;CHEMISTRY IS NOT PHOSPHOROTHIOATE. Review states verbatim (printed p39): 'Imetelstat sodium is a sodium salt of a 13-mer oligonucleotide N3'-->P5' thio-phosphoramidate conjugated with a lipid palmitoyl group attached to the 5' terminus through an aminoglycerol linker. The structure of imetelstat sodium includes thiophosphoramidate linkages, with sulfurizaton of the native phosphodiester, and replacement of the 3'-oxygen to provide a 3'-amino group.' Clin Pharm exec summary (printed p76) repeats: '13-mer N3'->P5' thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide with a palmitoyl lipid covalently attached by an aminoglycerol linker to the 5' thio-phosphate of the first nucleotide'. ps_count recorded as 0 because every internucleoside linkage is explicitly an N3'->P5' THIOPHOSPHORAMIDATE (sulfur present, but 3'-N not 3'-O; chemically distinct from a phosphorothioate diester linkage) - i.e. the molecule carries 12 sulfurised NP-S linkages plus a 5' thio-phosphate but ZERO phosphorothioate linkages. backbone_chemistry forced to 'mixed' only because the schema enum has no thio-phosphoramidate term; the true value is 'full_NPS (N3'->P5' thiophosphoramidate)'. MECHANISM CAVEAT: imetelstat thrombocytopenia is telomerase-inhibitor myelosuppression acting on megakaryocyte progenitors (CFU-MK), NOT the phosphorothioate-backbone platelet-binding/aggregation mechanism that drives the ASO class signal - the review itself attributes the toxicity to on-target telomerase inhibition in normal haematopoietic progenitors (printed p46-47) while separately noting that imetelstat's complement activation and aPTT prolongation 'reflect the well-characterized toxicity profile of the related phosphorothioate ODN class' (printed p55). Treat this compound as a mechanistic OUT-GROUP for PS-content modelling. NO NUCLEOTIDE SEQUENCE IS PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THIS 442-PAGE DOCUMENT (regex search for [ACGTU]{8,25} returned zero hits; the structural formula/molecular formula section is a bitmap/redacted) - sequence_5to3 therefore stays TBD, not recalled from memory. Mechanism: covalently-lipidated 13-mer that binds the template region of hTR, competitively inhibiting hTERT (printed p22, p76). Approved (regular approval), NDA 217779, review completion 24 May 2024. Human exposure anchor used for in-vitro grading: popPK-predicted Cmax 89.2 ug/mL at 7.1 mg/kg q4w, fraction unbound 0.06 (free Cmax ~5.35 ug/mL) - printed p48.
effect_vs_control: no effect on clonogenicity of normal MK progenitors, while malignant CFU-MK from essential thrombocythemia patients were dose-dependently suppressed
source_table: Applicant Figure 1 'Differential Effects of Imetelstat on Megakaryocytes Growth' and accompanying Applicant's Position text (Baerlocher, 2019) (printed p44-45)
notes_measurement: CONTRADICTORY NEGATIVE ROW, kept deliberately. The Applicant states 'imetelstat selectively suppressed spontaneous growth of malignant CFU-MK from patients with ET in a dose-dependent manner, while having no effect on clonogenicity of normal MK progenitors' - graded 0 on that stated null result for NORMAL megakaryocyte progenitors. THIS DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the Applicant's own Study GRN01 two pages later, in which normal human bone marrow CFU-MK were significantly inhibited at >=3.75 uM. The review does not reconcile the two. Any consumer should treat the normal-MK in-vitro picture as unresolved and weight GRN01 (a study the Applicant conducted, in normal marrow, with a stated concentration threshold) over the published ET-focused figure. readout_value and a numeric concentration are both TBD - Applicant Figure 1 is a bitmap dose-response plot with no printed values.

notes_measurement: DELIBERATELY GRADED 1, NOT 3. No numeric coagulation values reported.

source_table: p134, section 3.6 Effects Table, Unfavourable Effects row 'Haemorrhages'; narrative at p100 section 2.6
notes_measurement: GRADED 1, NOT 3, DESPITE THE WORD HAEMORRHAGE. notes_measurement: Verbatim: 'Re-initiation of inotersen in 16 recovered subjects with previous platelet decreases <75 x 10^9/L led anew to thrombocytopenic states in all but one of these subjects and subsequently to further treatment interruptions.' source_table: Combined Clinical/Biostatistical Review sec 4.4 'Nonclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology' (PDF p17)
notes_measurement: CROSS-SPECIES EXPOSURE-MARGIN row. Verbatim: 'Safety margins based on AUCs at the no observed adverse effect levels (NOAELs) for severe thrombocytopenia in monkeys and kidney toxicity in rats were <= ~2-fold, suggesting monitoring in humans may be warranted.' Graded 3 because the severe (fatal-in-animals) thrombocytopenia NOAEL sits at or below ~2x the human clinical AUC - i.e. the severe effect occurs at essentially clinical exposure, which is the animal analogue of the rubric's grade-3 'at or below therapeutic plasma concentration' criterion. Human reference exposure: Cmax 12.1 ug/mL at 300 mg SC weekly.

Verbatim: 'five other animals across the three lowest dose groups showed perivascular mixed cell infiltration in multiple organs ... and (in 4/5 animals) with moderate reductions in platelet counts (49-70%, compared to baseline).' So 4 of 5 animals in the three lowest dose groups had moderate platelet reductions. Grade 2 (source's own word: 'moderate'). Numeric mg/kg doses not stated in this document -> TBD. Together with the severe cases in the two highest dose groups this establishes a dose-response across the monkey study.

notes_measurement: Verbatim: 'A higher proportion of patients in the inotersen group (60 of 112, 54%) had a confirmed decrease in the postbaseline platelet count to less than 140,000 per cubic millimeter than in the placebo group (8 of 60, 13%).' Caveat recorded rather than hidden: crossing 140 does not establish that counts stayed >=100, and the deeper bands (<100, <75) are NOT in the main text -- they live in Table S10, which could not be retrieved (NEJM Supplementary Appendix is paywalled and the PMC supplement mirror is reCAPTCHA-gated).

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Importantly, further investigation ruled out a heparin-induced thrombocytopenia-type mechanism and effects on platelet production'
notes_measurement: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE, and the most useful row in this paper for anyone modelling mechanism: the authors explicitly exclude both a HIT-type mechanism and a production/megakaryocyte defect, leaving peripheral antibody-mediated destruction. Grade 0 because no megakaryocyte or production abnormality was observed -- this is a genuine explicit no-effect finding at the stated locus, not an absence of mention. readout_value is TBD because the paper gives no assay, no numbers, and no supporting data for the exclusion; the claim is qualitative.

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'No cases of thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of less than 50,000 per cubic millimeter occurred after the institution of weekly platelet monitoring'
notes_measurement: EXPLICIT ZERO, and it is evidence. Had events occurred in this band (<50x10^9/L) the row would have carried grade 3; it is recorded as grade 0 so the severe band stays findable. Important interpretation: this zero measures the effect of a risk-mitigation protocol (weekly platelet monitoring plus dose-stopping rules), not an absence of intrinsic hazard -- the same compound produced three <25x10^9/L events before monitoring was intensified. The denominator and duration of the post-monitoring period are not given in the main text, hence exposure_duration is qualitative.

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Platelet counts in 2 of these 3 patients returned to baseline or near-baseline levels after discontinuation of the trial regimen and treatment with glucocorticoids. The third patient presented with an intracranial hemorrhage and died before treatment could be initiated'
notes_measurement: recovered_after_discontinuation. Graded on the severity of the underlying event (<25x10^9/L, grade 3) -- reversibility does not downgrade an event that was life-threatening while it lasted, and one of the three did not recover. Glucocorticoid responsiveness is one of the two pieces of evidence the authors give for an immune-mediated mechanism (the other being anti-platelet IgG, next row).

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'There was some evidence of an immune-mediated mechanism in the severe events, as indicated by recovery with glucocorticoid treatment and the presence of antiplatelet IgG in each of the 3 patients'
notes_measurement: Anti-platelet IgG detected in all three patients with severe thrombocytopenia. Grade 3 is taken directly from the rubric clause 'immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with confirmed anti-platelet antibodies'. This row is the mechanistic core of the rare/severe/idiosyncratic pole of the bimodal endpoint and should not be collapsed with the mild count-decline rows. Assay, titre, and timing are not given in the main text.

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of less than 25,000 per cubic millimeter occurred in 3 patients (3%) who received inotersen' (also stated in Discussion, paragraph 2)
notes_measurement: THE CANONICAL SEVERE ANCHOR. <25x10^9/L is CTCAE grade 4 -> schema grade 3. Graded on the severity of the event, not on the smallness of the 3% incidence. One of the three patients died of intracranial haemorrhage. The paper does not tabulate a placebo figure at this threshold, so no explicit-zero control row is emitted for it (absence of a statement is not a grade-0 datum).

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Two patients in the inotersen group had a dose reduction to 150 mg weekly because of decreases in platelet counts'
notes_measurement: GRADE 2 ANCHOR, and one of the few clean ones in the clinical literature for this endpoint: the rubric assigns grade 2 to a platelet decline 'requiring monitoring, dose interruption, or dose reduction', and this is an actioned dose reduction (300 -> 150 mg weekly) taken specifically for falling platelets. The platelet counts that triggered the reduction are not stated, so severity is inferred from the clinical action, which is precisely what the rubric asks for at this grade.

source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 4, final sentence: 'The incidence of hemorrhages was similar in the two groups'
notes_measurement: GRADED 0, NOT 3, and this is the deliberate application of the schema's bleeding-attribution rule. An aggregate bleeding rate that is similar to placebo is a background rate, not a drug-induced platelet injury; grading it 3 on the word 'hemorrhage' would manufacture a severe event out of a null result. The one bleed that IS attributable to thrombocytopenia (the fatal intracranial haemorrhage) is captured on its own rows at grade 3. is_platelet_specific FALSE because this aggregate term is not platelet-attributed. No numerator or denominator is printed, hence readout_value TBD.

notes_measurement: SECONDARY CITATION — PARENT MUST DEDUPE against the primary NEURO-TTR publication. Verbatim: 'Another study testing an ASO (inotersen) to inhibit the transthyretin (TTR) protein production in 172 patients with hereditary TTR amyloidosis in a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study (NEURO-TTR) reported on three serious adverse events of thrombocytopenia, of whom two patients recovered and one patient died due to intracranial haemorrhage.' GRADE 3: serious adverse events of thrombocytopenia, one fatal — squarely in the rubric's severe band. The denominator 172 is the whole trial population as stated here; the source does NOT break it down by arm, so no arm-level incidence is computed. Dose and duration TBD — not stated in this source. Unlike ref 7, reference 4 is correctly and completely cited here.

source_table: Discussion, paragraph added during manuscript review
notes_measurement: QUALITATIVE ROW - no event count, no platelet value, no dose is given. Source text verbatim: 'During the review of this manuscript, we reported that severe thrombocytopenic events occurred in two placebo-controlled phase 3 studies with two different 2'MOE chimeric ASOs, IONIS-TTRRx and volanesorsen... we have never previously experienced severe thrombocytopenic events in any clinical trial including long term studies. While these trials remain blinded and investigations to understand the causes of these events are still in progress, we do know that the events are not due to prolonged exposure as all events occurred 4-9 months after initiation of therapy.' Graded 3 on the authors' explicit characterisation 'severe thrombocytopenic events'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT for downstream use: the trials were still BLINDED at time of writing, so drug attribution was not established in this source; the authors flag infections, concomitant drugs and the underlying diseases as possible contributors. This row is the phase-3 counterpart to the null healthy-volunteer result in Table 2 and is the single most consequential statement in the article for this endpoint.

notes_measurement: HUMAN clinical row — the priority class for this dataset. One subject in the Phase I programme had a platelet decrease explicitly described as reversible. GRADING RATIONALE (non-obvious, please read): the abstract gives NO platelet count, no nadir, no percent decline, no denominator and no route/dose attribution, so the grade rests only on the qualitative descriptors available. Grade 1 is assigned because the event is stated to be reversible, no intervention, dose interruption, dose reduction, bleeding or discontinuation is described, and the paper's own conclusion is that the drug was "generally well tolerated intravenously and subcutaneously". Grade 1 should be treated as a FLOOR, not a confirmed ceiling: if the full text (inaccessible - see extraction_notes) shows a count in the 50-99 x10^9/L band or a dose interruption, this row becomes grade 2, and grade 3 if <50 x10^9/L or antibody-mediated. dose_or_conc_value/unit are TBD rather than the printed 0.1-6 mg/kg i.v. band because the abstract does not say whether the affected subject was in the i.v. escalation or an s.c. cohort - assigning the band would be an invented attribution. readout_unit is n_subjects rather than pct_incidence because the abstract states no total N, so an incidence percentage cannot be computed without fabrication. EXCLUSION LINE: ISIS 104838 targets TNF-alpha mRNA and has no intended antiplatelet or antithrombotic pharmacology, so this platelet decrease is an UNINTENDED effect and is correctly in scope; none of the on-target-antithrombotic exclusion (ARC1779 / pegnivacogin class) applies here.

notes_measurement: HIGHEST cumulative exposure in this programme - 400 mg/month - and the row whose source sentence names platelet count directly rather than by programme summary. notes_measurement: Haemorrhagic event ATTRIBUTED to thrombocytopenia, which is what the rubric requires for grade 3 (not the keyword alone). As printed: 'Following blood collection on Day 269, it was noted that that the venipuncture site bled for ~30 min after sample collection and became severely swollen'; and 'Postmortem analysis revealed widespread multifocal hemorrhage (presumably secondary to thrombocytopenia)'. Gross necropsy correlates: red discoloration of bone marrow, heart (hemorrhage) and gastric mucosa (hemorrhage) (review p100). Animal died (moribund sacrifice), independently satisfying grade 3.

notes_measurement: GRADE 0 DESPITE A SIGNIFICANT CHANGE: the direction is an INCREASE (reactive thrombocytosis), not thrombocytopenia, so the thrombocytopenia rubric scores it 0. Table legend: 'Mean treated value > control mean value displayed as fold increase'; the dagger marks p<0.01 vs untreated control. Reviewer text: 'a dose-related [increase] in platelet count in males'. Corroborated in the supervisory memo dose table (review p2), which lists 'increased platelets' as a 25 mg/kg/wk finding at ~1x human AUC. This is the direct opposite of the monkey response to the same drug and is a useful species-discordance signal.

notes_measurement: HUMAN IN-VITRO ROW — the second-priority class for this dataset. WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AND THE THREE ON-TARGET ROWS DO NOT (the exclusion line, stated as instructed): pegnivacogin's reductions in ADP-induced CD62P (100% vs 89.79+/-4.04%, p=0.027, n=9), PAC-1 binding (100% vs 83.02+/-4.08%, p=0.010, n=11), LTA aggregation (97.71+/-5.30% vs 66.53+/-9.92%, p=0.013, n=10) and residual aggregation in RADAR patients after 1 mg/kg IV (100% vs 43.21+/-8.23%, p=0.020) are all DECREASES produced BY DESIGN — FIXa inhibition lowers thrombin generation, thrombin is 'a major platelet activator' (the paper's own Background), and the paper's Conclusion frames the result as 'a promising antithrombotic strategy'. That is intended anticoagulant pharmacology, is excluded per the anti-FIXa/anti-vWF rule, and is NOT entered as toxicity in any direction. THE ANIVAMERSEN CONDITION IS DIFFERENT AND IS IN SCOPE: with the aptamer's on-target activity neutralised by its complementary antidote, the oligonucleotides are still present in human whole blood, and the source reports NO platelet-activation signal — i.e. an explicit negative for a TARGET-INDEPENDENT (unintended) oligonucleotide-platelet interaction, which is precisely the hazard this dataset exists to capture for PS-ASOs and aptamers. GRADE 0 per the rubric's in-vitro column ('No activation, aggregation, or binding above vehicle control at tested concentration'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE GRADE: the abstract phrases this as absence of ATTENUATION ('was not attenuated' / 'negated'), which asserts return to the control level rather than explicitly asserting 'no increase above control'; no increase is reported anywhere in the abstract, and no numbers are printed for this condition, so readout_value is TBD. If full text shows a supra-control CD62P rise under anivamersen this row becomes grade 1. readout_unit follows the abstract's own convention for these readouts (control normalised to 100%); the value itself was not printed. dose_or_conc_value is TBD, not the patients' 1 mg/kg bolus — the abstract gives no in-vitro pegnivacogin (or anivamersen) concentration, and importing the clinical dose would be an invented attribution. Full text inaccessible (paywalled) — see extraction_notes.

source_table: p99 narrative, section 'Discontinuations due to decrease in platelet counts'
notes_measurement: Across studies CS6, CS16 and CS2, 5 patients had platelet reductions to <50,000/mm3, 2 of which were declines to <25,000/mm3, 3 of which led to permanent discontinuation. notes_measurement: Median, IQR 162.0-211.8, n=4, at week 36 on q14d maintenance. source_table: Results 3.4 'Platelet Aggregation Analysis' (Methods 2.5)
notes_measurement: HUMAN EX-VIVO PLATELET FUNCTION under a marketed 2'-MOE PS ASO - the row type NCATS asked for. Agonist ADP 1.8 uM; Born turbidimetric aggregometry on platelet-rich plasma, CHRONO-LOG 700 aggregometer, at week 36 of volanesorsen. Prespecified normality criterion (Methods 2.5): >=50% light transmission within 3 min indicates NO impairment of aggregation; 62% clears it. n=4 patients vs 4 matched healthy controls, no significant difference. Graded 0. Interpretive value: volanesorsen lowers the platelet COUNT by ~34% without impairing the FUNCTION of the platelets that remain - so count and function dissociate, and an in-vitro activation/aggregation assay is not a surrogate for the count endpoint.

source_table: Table 3 'Thrombin generation analysis in FCs patients vs. controls'
notes_measurement: Mean +/- SD, calibrated automated thrombogram (CAT) with PPP-reagent LOW, week 36. is_platelet_specific FALSE - adjacent coagulation readout. Graded 0 because the difference is not statistically significant and the authors report all values within normal range. WORTH FLAGGING despite grade 0: the point estimate is ~33% lower than controls and the authors single it out ('an interesting difference in the amount of thrombin obtained'); with n=4 the study is not powered to exclude a real effect, so this is a null result from a very small sample, not a demonstrated absence. readout_unit is the conventional CAT unit for ETP; the source's Table 3 prints the number without a unit.

source_table: Discussion, p540-541 narrative ('a classic heparin-induced mechanism for thrombocytopenia was excluded, as were antisense-mediated effects on platelet production')
notes_measurement: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE — grade 0. A production-side (megakaryocyte) mechanism was excluded, pointing to peripheral platelet clearance instead. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: this is a bare assertion in the Discussion; the paper describes NO assay, criteria, bone-marrow examination or supporting data for the exclusion and cites no reference for it, so readout_value is the qualitative word 'excluded' and effect_vs_control is TBD. tissue is recorded as bone_marrow because that is the compartment the claim concerns, but no bone-marrow sampling is reported. CONVERGENCE ACROSS SOURCES: this agrees with the independent EMA EPAR finding of no haematopoietic/bone-marrow toxicity in cynomolgus monkeys, so two independent documents concur that the mechanism is peripheral rather than central — a useful human-to-animal extrapolation anchor.

source_table: Discussion, p540-541 narrative ('Nearly all the patients received an injection of heparin at the beginning of the trial and at approximately 26 weeks to enable measurement of LPL activity, but a classic heparin-induced mechanism for thrombocytopenia was excluded')
notes_measurement: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE — grade 0, and an important confounder-exclusion specific to this trial. Nearly all patients received heparin TWICE (at baseline and ~week 26) because post-heparin LPL activity was an eligibility/assessment measure, creating a genuine risk that heparin-induced thrombocytopenia would be mistaken for drug-induced thrombocytopenia; the authors state classic HIT was excluded. LIMITATION: no anti-PF4/heparin antibody assay, 4T score, timing analysis or other criteria are described and no data are shown, so readout_value is the qualitative word 'excluded'. Recorded because ruling out HIT is what licenses attributing the platelet signal to the oligonucleotide itself. Note that PF4 is the antigen in classic HIT and PS-oligonucleotide/PF4 interaction is a known mechanism of interest for this endpoint, but this paper does not address that possibility.

system_model: patient_cohort (APPROACH phase 3 RCT, NCT02211209, familial chylomicronemia syndrome, patients with the most severe events)
source_table: Discussion, p540-541 narrative ('The underlying mechanisms responsible for the declines in platelet levels are not clear at present... There was some evidence for associated immunologic response in the most severe events')
notes_measurement: QUALITATIVE MECHANISTIC ROW, graded 3 on the severity of the events it refers to (the CTCAE grade-4 cases). GRADING CAVEAT STATED EXPLICITLY: this does NOT satisfy the rubric's 'immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with CONFIRMED anti-platelet antibodies' criterion, because NO anti-platelet antibody result of any kind is reported anywhere in this paper — the authors say only that there was 'some evidence for associated immunologic response', with no assay, titre, numbers or reference given, and they state plainly that the underlying mechanism 'is not clear at present'. readout_value therefore carries the source's hedged wording verbatim and effect_vs_control is TBD. This is the strongest support this paper offers for the rare, severe, immune-mediated limb of the endpoint's bimodal presentation, and it is weak; the two grade-4 patients' clinical response to glucocorticoids and IVIG is circumstantially consistent with an immune mechanism but is not presented as evidence by the authors. FOR CONTRAST, the EMA EPAR reports that anti-drug-antibody status did NOT increase the incidence of platelet decrease (78% ADA-negative vs 38% ADA-positive) and that anti-platelet antibodies were undetectable in 7 of 8 affected monkeys — both arguing against an antibody-mediated mechanism.

notes_measurement: QUALITATIVE ROW — readout_value carries the source's own wording verbatim. Graded 1 because the characterisation describes the common, mild, reversible, dose-dependent limb of this endpoint's bimodal presentation, which is the grade-1 phenotype; the rare severe idiosyncratic limb is captured at grade 3 in the band rows. This paper offers NO plasma-concentration/exposure-response analysis for platelets — the EMA EPAR remains the only source in the dataset reporting the Ctrough/AUC relationship, the ~30%-below-baseline plateau and the body-weight association.

source_table: Results, 'Safety' subsection, p539 narrative ('9 discontinued the trial because of adverse events that occurred during treatment - 5 because of platelet decreases'); restated in Discussion p541
notes_measurement: Graded 3: treatment discontinuation for a platelet event is an explicit grade-3 criterion. RECONCILIATION: these 5 comprise the 2 patients with grade-4 thrombocytopenia whose treatment was discontinued plus the 3 patients with lesser (CTCAE grade 1 or 2) platelet decreases withdrawn on site-investigator concern — 2 + 3 = 5 exactly, which the paper's separate narrative statements confirm. Of 14 volanesorsen patients who did not complete the 52-week trial, 9 discontinued for treatment-emergent AEs (5 platelet, 4 other: injection-site reaction and fatigue; fatigue; chills and sweating; generalized erythema), 4 withdrew voluntarily and 1 was withdrawn for non-adherence. Placebo: 2 patients did not complete, neither for a platelet event. There were no deaths during the trial. AGREES exactly with EMA EPAR (5/33, 15%).

notes_measurement: EXPLICIT ZERO — grade 0. Had events occurred this would have carried GRADE 3 (<50 x10^9/L). Stated independently at THREE loci in the paper (Abstract, Results, Discussion), which is why it is retained as its own row; arithmetically it is the union of the two 'after' zeros in the 25,000-50,000 and 0-25,000 Table 4 bands, so DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT it with those rows when computing event totals. source_table: Results, 'Safety' subsection, p539 narrative ('After these rules were implemented, no patients had platelet-count declines to less than 50,000 per microliter, and no platelet-related dose discontinuations occurred'); restated in Discussion p540
notes_measurement: EXPLICIT ZERO — grade 0. Had discontinuations occurred this row would have carried GRADE 3. Together with the zero counts in the two severe Table 4 bands after implementation, this is the paper's evidence that a monitoring-and-dose-adjustment algorithm can manage volanesorsen's platelet toxicity without stopping therapy. IMPORTANT COUNTERPOINT: the EMA EPAR reports that in the longer open-label extension 9 patients discontinued for platelet decreases and 4 developed severe thrombocytopenia DESPITE the dose algorithm being in force from the outset, so this trial's post-implementation zero should not be over-generalised to longer-term exposure.

notes_measurement: Graded 2: <100,000/uL is the threshold that triggered dose-frequency reduction under the trial's own platelet algorithm, i.e. it required intervention. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION WITHIN THIS PAPER: the ABSTRACT states '15 of 33 patients in the volanesorsen group had such levels', whereas the Results text AND Table 4 both give 16. Table 4 is internally consistent at 16 (its bands 6+7+1+2 sum to 16, and its before/after split 10+6 sums to 16), so 16/33 is recorded here as authoritative and the abstract's 15 is treated as an error rather than given its own row. Separately, EMA EPAR Table 37 prints 15/32 (46.9%) — its numerator coincidentally equals the abstract's, but over a denominator of 32, not 33.

source_table: Results, 'Safety' subsection, p539 narrative ('Dose reduction of volanesorsen occurred in 13 patients; dose reductions in 9 of those patients occurred because of decreases in platelet counts')
notes_measurement: Graded 2: dose reduction required is an explicit grade-2 criterion. 9 of 33 volanesorsen patients; the paper prints counts, not a percentage, so readout_value carries the count and no percentage was back-computed. Dose reduction meant a change from 300 mg weekly to 300 mg every 2 weeks. The paper gives NO placebo comparator for dose reduction, so effect_vs_control records the within-arm denominator only. Related context from the same paper: of the 19 volanesorsen patients who completed the full 52-week treatment period, only 6 remained on 300 mg weekly throughout; in the other 13, dosing frequency was reduced, treatment was paused, or both.

source_table: Results, 'Safety' subsection, p539 narrative ('the two patients reached normal platelet counts 23 and 33 days after discontinuation of the drug')
notes_measurement: Graded 3 on the severity of the underlying events (both patients had CTCAE grade 4 thrombocytopenia, <25,000/uL). readout_value carries BOTH individual patient values separated by ';' rather than an invented mean. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON INTERPRETATION: recovery is NOT attributable to drug withdrawal alone — both patients received glucocorticoids and one also received IV immune globulin (regimens detailed in the 0-<25,000/uL band row), so these are recovery-with-treatment times, not natural washout kinetics. effect_direction 'increase' refers to the recovering platelet count. The Discussion notes more generally that decreases in platelet levels 'were reversible with an interruption in dosing'.

source_table: Results, 'Safety' subsection, p539 narrative ('Three other patients with lesser grades (grade 1 or 2) of decreased platelet counts were withdrawn from the trial because of concerns on the part of the site investigators')
notes_measurement: GRADING TENSION MADE EXPLICIT: graded 3 because withdrawal from treatment for a platelet event is an explicit grade-3 criterion in the rubric, BUT the underlying platelet decline in these 3 patients was only CTCAE grade 1 or 2 and the withdrawals were precautionary decisions by site investigators rather than protocol-threshold breaches. A consumer modelling event severity rather than treatment impact may prefer to treat these as grade 1-2; the distinction is recorded here rather than silently resolved. SUBSET WARNING: these 3 patients are a subset of the 5 in the 'discontinuation_due_to_low_platelet_count_count' row — do not sum. The Discussion attributes these withdrawals to 'the combination of an unexpected, potentially serious level of thrombocytopenia occurring during the trial and the lack of a prespecified protocol for responding to it in a timely manner', which 'led to patient and investigator uncertainty'.

notes_measurement: CONTROL-ARM ROW — filter on dose_or_conc_value == '0' before joining grade to design features. Graded 1 on what was observed (8 placebo patients genuinely had confirmed nadirs below the LLN), per the rubric's explicit instruction that control arms are graded on the observed band. These 8 patients ALL fell in the 100,000-<140,000 band; every deeper band is 0 in the placebo arm. effect_direction 'decrease' refers to the platelet count relative to the normal limit, not to a drug effect. This substantial placebo rate is a genuine disease-background signal: the Discussion cites a natural-history study of FCS patients in which 55.2% had thrombocytopenia on at least one occasion over up to 15 years. Before/after split 4 before / 4 after — flat, as expected for an untreated arm. AGREES exactly with EMA EPAR Table 37 (8/33, 24.2%).

notes_measurement: GRADING RATIONALE: epistaxis is mucocutaneous ('platelet-type') bleeding, elevated 5/33 versus 0/33 placebo, so it is retained as a platelet-specific bleeding signal. LIMITATION: the paper does NOT report any per-patient correlation between epistaxis and platelet nadir, so attribution to thrombocytopenia specifically is inferred from the term's nature and the zero placebo rate, and is not stated by the source. Consistent with existing dataset convention for epistaxis rows.

notes_measurement: GRADING RATIONALE (bleeding is graded on attribution, not on the keyword): petechiae are the classic cutaneous manifestation of thrombocytopenia and occurred in 4/33 volanesorsen patients versus 0/33 placebo, so this is a drug-associated platelet-type bleeding signal rather than a background rate. It is nonetheless graded 1, NOT 3, because Table 4's footnote states explicitly that NO PATIENT IN EITHER ARM HAD A MAJOR BLEEDING EVENT, and the Results narrative confirms no major bleeding even in the two grade-4 patients. Grade 3 requires a haemorrhagic event attributable to thrombocytopenia; a minor cutaneous manifestation with no major bleeding anywhere in the trial does not meet it. Consistent with existing dataset convention for petechiae rows.

notes_measurement: EXPLICIT ZERO — grade 0. Had events occurred this band would have carried GRADE 3 (CTCAE grade 4). No further grade-4 thrombocytopenia occurred after the enhanced platelet-monitoring program was implemented, despite continued dosing. This is the key risk-management datum of the trial and the direct evidence behind the platelet-monitoring requirements later imposed on the marketed product.
